title: Compound
description: One substance that takes part in a reaction (spec 3.3): a compound such as sodium chloride, or an element as it actually occurs, such as chlorine gas (Cl2) or sodium metal. Every displayed value is a Fact. See verification/methodology.md.

element.description: Set when this substance is a pure element (Cl2, Na): the element page it belongs to. The gate checks the formula contains only that element.

nistId.description: The substance's exact NIST WebBook ID, e.g. C7647145. Lookups are by ID, never by name: names and formulas return the wrong entry too often.

formula.description: The formula as chemists usually write it, e.g. "NaCl" or "Ca(OH)2". PubChem and NIST list atoms in another order ("ClNa"); that spelling goes in source.asWritten, and the gate checks both contain the same atoms.

standardState.description: The substance's state at 25 °C and normal pressure.

formationEnthalpies.description: Standard enthalpy of formation (kJ/mol) for each phase the reactions need, from the NIST WebBook. For an element in its standard state the value is 0 by definition (rule zero-for-element-in-standard-state). Empty when the WebBook has no value.

hazards.description: GHS hazard statements from PubChem, only those more than half of the notifiers report (decided 2026-11-15). Empty when there are none.

reportedBy.description: Share of PubChem's notifiers that report this statement, in percent. Must be above 50.

phase.description: s solid, l liquid, g gas.
